item: The best-ranked strategy is positive but not repeatable across weeks
detail: M1 gains 1.74 points per game on average with a 95% bootstrap interval that excludes zero, but its skill is positive in only 5 of 7 out-of-sample weeks. A sign test on that 5-of-7 split gives p = 0.4531, which chance produces routinely. The leaderboard rank is therefore a description of 89 games, not evidence that M1 will beat the reference line going forward. Published on the leaderboard as the skill-versus-luck columns; not suppressed, because suppressing it would hide the uncertainty.
action_requested: Decide whether to keep publishing ranks alongside the luck columns (recommended path P07 option A).

item: Nine 2026 games are at neutral sites but the model added home-field to all of them
detail: The 2026 season has a record nine international games (NFL Football Operations, SRC-72). The results dataset carried no neutral-site column, so the fit and the naive reference line added the home-field term for the designated home team even though the game was not in its stadium. On the 89 out-of-sample games this changed no rounded output, because only two affected games fall inside the evaluation window (wk5 PHI at JAX, wk7 PIT at NO); the measurable effect is on the Week 11 Mexico City line (fair margin 2.5 to 2.9; model-minus-reference -6.2 to -3.3). Remediated with a neutral_site column threaded through fit(), predict() and ref_line().
action_requested: Week 11 MIN at SF is modelled as neutral. All 137 completed rows carry a BLANK neutral_site value because this session did not re-open every schedule page to confirm each stadium; nothing was inferred. The historical fit therefore still treats those games as home games, so the no-op above is a reported finding, not a correction. Open item for review: confirm the nine individual games against a stadium field before the historical column is populated.

item: C09 published a Fisher correlation interval for a regression slope
detail: C09 is the slope of actual margin on predicted margin (0.885, SE 0.280, n 89). The register applied the Pearson-r interval (Fisher z, SE = 1/sqrt(n-3)) and a p-value for r, publishing 0.830-0.923 and p 0.0000. Recomputed with the coefficient's own t interval: 0.328-1.443, p = 0.683 against a slope of 1.0. Remediated by add_slope(), which uses estimate +/- t(0.975, df)*SE and tests against the null the question actually asks about. Closes handoff REQ-8a-1, logged by session 8a0bf37e.
action_requested: Published interval and p-value replaced; point estimate 0.885 unchanged. The correct reading is that the data do not distinguish the slope from 1.0, which is the opposite of the previous p 0.0000.
